announcements.title: v2.8.0: Free-lane shaping layer aligned with reference gateway v1.4.6, one-click engine follow-up
announcements.html:
2.8.0 replaces the anonymous free lane's request shaping wholesale with a file-by-file port of the reference gateway opencode2api v1.4.6. All client tools are renamed to opaque wire names before going upstream (no foreign client's tool vocabulary is ever sent), the official 2.1 CLI's 13 verbatim tool definitions and the full official system prompt are included; every request carries a brand-new 40-hex project id, so quota no longer crowds into the shared global bucket; endpoints move to the 2.1 client's family paths; session minting uses a slow clock, so dates always fall inside the window the upstream accepts. The previous rounds of "shape all correct, still 429" recurrences all stemmed from these three classes of gate, and the port resolves them together.

The bundled Magpie engine follows upstream's 6a900e0d of 2026-10-31, the build now uses the same trimming flags as upstream releases, and the gzip payload drops from 45.3 MB to 27.2 MB — the release package is 77 files, back within the old upgrader's 80-file limit. A new update:magpie command: from now on an engine follow-up is a single command, with automatic rollback on failure. A problem on the engine settings page where a numeric input in a narrow panel was cut in half is fixed in the same release. npm test gains a release-bundle freshness guard: change the source without re-bundling and the test goes red on the spot.

This release publishes only the plugin package; the desktop app version and installers are not updated with it. The npm channel simultaneously publishes @ebony-vinyl/dsh-our-free-model@2.8.0; the bare-named dsh-our-free-model on npm is still a third-party package — do not install it.

announcements.title: v2.7.4: Community fixes merged and a stability sweep
announcements.html:
2.7.4 merges 19 community fix PRs and 8 local fixes, covering forwarding, channels, the workbench and the upgrade chain. Streaming tool-call frames now include id/name and consecutive index values, Responses streams include sequence_number; when an upstream 5xx has an empty response body it now says which layer failed and notes that the request contained images; keepalive comment frames no longer keep an idle dead line alive indefinitely; transient network failures carry a code and can be retried normally.

Concurrent sessions no longer share a global session; -vl vision models are no longer labelled as plain text; empty-string enum members in Gemini tool schemas are stripped. On the channel side, fixes for the trae cache hit rate being constantly 0, channel account "Test" constantly failing, and the session picker not refreshing after a channel model is hidden; EAC sign-in supports the Windows system proxy.

The workbench fixes "startup failed" caused by Windows reserved port ranges and losing the collapse button at the moment of expanding; 0600 permissions on private files on Windows actually take effect via icacls; pnpm-managed installs refuse in-app upgrades and hand them back to the original installation method. This release publishes only the plugin package; the desktop app version and installers are not updated with it.

New npm channel: this repository now publishes the scoped @ebony-vinyl/dsh-our-free-model, from the same source and version as the Release tarball, installable with dsh plugin --profile web add @ebony-vinyl/dsh-our-free-model@2.7.4. The bare-named dsh-our-free-model on npm is still a third-party package — do not install it.

announcements.title: v2.7.3: Free-lane compatibility, account queue account-switching and security upgrades
announcements.html:
2.7.3 updates the DSH plugin side. The free lane adopts the Bun transport, completes environment information and migrates old session mappings; reversible tool aliases are added for the real DSH toolset, preserving tool descriptions, parameters and host execution ability. Account channels support switching accounts within the same channel and model for explicit queueing responses, and fix anonymous-slot rotation, account ownership and the auth-renewal budget.

When the client cancels or disconnects, upstream connections and concurrency slots are released promptly; a cancellation during a proxy handshake is also cleaned up immediately. When the host cannot hot-reload safely, the upgrade files prompt for a restart to take effect after installation, and managed installs remain managed by the host. The English and Chinese READMEs are synced to community group 12.

Prerequisite: the default OpenCode free inference requires the user to install native Bun themselves; the plugin does not download it automatically; use OUR_FREE_MODEL_BUN to specify a path. This release publishes only the plugin package; the desktop app version and installers are not updated with it. Compatibility fixes do not lift the upstream's actual quota, region or account limits.

announcements.title: v2.7.1: WorkBuddy China edition / international edition and Huawei Cloud channels fully removed
announcements.html: 2.7.1 tightens the channel exclusion. WorkBuddy China edition (workbuddy, also known as CodeBuddy), international edition (workbuddy-ai), Huawei Cloud MaaS (huaweicloud, including Token Plan) and Huawei Cloud CodeArts cannot be added, signed in to, or installed via the plugin marketplace on either the plugin side or the desktop side. This release covers the two previously uncovered aliases CodeBuddy and CodeArts, and adds a usage notice and disclaimer making clear that this plugin is a personal learning project, does not provide these channels, and that use of third-party channels is unrelated to this team.

announcements.title: v2.7.0: The desktop side gains the same model workbench
announcements.html: 2.7.0 gives the desktop side the same model workbench too. The desktop console adds a "Model Workbench" page, embedding the same magpie engine as the plugin side: the same channel and account management, the same model list, the same theme following and full screen. Once the workbench starts, its models merge into the aggregate list and appear in the model picker alongside the subscription lanes; the channel exclusion policy (WorkBuddy and Huawei Cloud) is consistent on both sides. The desktop installer bundles this engine binary.

announcements.title: v2.6.0: Model workbench, subscription lanes and native Gemini access; WorkBuddy and Huawei Cloud channels removed
announcements.html:
2.6.0 updates the DSH plugin side. Adds the model workbench (embedded engine, theme following, branding), subscription lanes (Codex/Claude/Gemini/API import and local-machine discovery, quota queries and refresh rotation, credentials written to disk at 0600 with redacted output), three smart routing strategies and nested routing groups, native Gemini generateContent/streamGenerateContent/countTokens endpoints, Anthropic tool_choice pass-through, and an interactive client launcher; the desktop side adds four management pages for clients and subscriptions, the resource library, routing groups and aggregate channels.

This version does not provide WorkBuddy or Huawei Cloud MaaS channels, consistently on the plugin and desktop sides; the first open shows a usage notice and disclaimer once on the settings page / console, after which it can be viewed again from the footer or sidebar. Also fixes turn double-counting when a composite chain goes through a subscription model, and the release manifest being rebuilt alongside the source.

announcements.title: v2.5.9: Account channels streamlined, legacy resources cleaned up and community group info synced
announcements.html: 2.5.9 updates the DSH plugin side. Cleans up account channels that are no longer provided, along with their sign-in, request, page entry, dependency and documentation, keeping 10 account channels, the anonymous free channel and EAC. Syncs the desktop side's channel resources and deletes legacy frontend files; shared storage and backups keep historical-format compatibility. The README updates community group 5's QR code and group number.

announcements.title: v2.5.8: Update retry, Qoder thinking levels and tool-turn reasoning return fixed
announcements.html: 2.5.8 updates the DSH plugin side. Fixes the Windows update backup rename retry and reuses verified download staging; Qoder thinking levels are sorted by intensity; Chat tool turns preserve the reasoning content returned by the client. The EAC DeepSeek Flash display name gains the 1017 marker.

announcements.title: v2.5.6: Plugin sponsor card streamlined, free models and EAC page shown uniformly
announcements.html: 2.5.6 updates the DSH plugin side. A compact Beichen API sponsor card is shown uniformly at the top of the free-model and EAC model pages, with copy updated to "invites earn a ten percent cashback". Removes the "Ads from sponsors" navigation and detail route, keeping the card and its view link; also fixes old modules continuing to run because hot-reload dependencies were not refreshed on some paths.

announcements.title: v2.5.5: Community group block and splash sponsor ad removed on the plugin side
announcements.html: 2.5.5 updates only the DSH plugin side. The community group, group number and copy button in the sponsor notes have been deleted, and the sponsor splash ad that popped up automatically when the desktop plugin started is turned off. The sponsor page entry and invite-code feature are kept; the standalone service and desktop shell are not updated with this version.

announcements.title: v2.5.4: New desktop side optimized, plugin-side UI and ads optimized
announcements.html:
2.5.4 optimizes the new desktop side and the plugin-side UI, and improves ad display.

  • The desktop side improves the sponsor entry, light and dark themes and narrow-window display.
  • The plugin side adds an "Ads from sponsors" menu; the full notes and attached images can be viewed at any time.
  • The daily announcement is shown once per local date and can be collapsed at any time; fixes announcements not displaying in the host settings dialog, with Esc collapsing only the announcement and returning focus to the menu.

The plugin, standalone service and Windows desktop side are all updated to 2.5.4. For managed installs, update the trusted tarball; Windows users should first quit the old program in the tray, then install the new version.

announcements.title: v2.5.3 urgent fix: EAC 60-second no-output cutoff removed
announcements.html:
2.5.3 removes the EAC 60-second no-valid-output cutoff added in 2.5.2. Queueing, silent thinking and heartbeat-only waits are no longer terminated early by that rule. The progressTimeoutMs in old configurations no longer takes effect; user cancellation and the existing transport disconnect detection remain in effect.

This release did not change the OpenCode fingerprint or admission logic; the anonymous channel's 403 / LANE_LOCKED still needs to be investigated separately from EAC wait issues.

announcements.title: v2.5.2: Upgrade, account sign-in and streaming error fixes; Windows installer updated

link.label: View release notes and download artifacts

announcements.html:
2.5.2 has released the plugin tarball and the Windows x64 full installer. Fixes update failures caused by GitHub API rate limiting, old module caches, repeated announcement notifications, desktop account sign-in and erroneous request cooldowns; completes system prompt, blank response and streaming error handling.

Adds model hiding, chain capability intersection display and a standalone-service LAN inference relay. For package-manager installs, use distribution: managed and update the trusted tarball path.

The anonymous channel's upstream 403 / LANE_LOCKED is not claimed to be fixed. Real availability still depends on upstream admission, quota and the network; an EAC 60-second no-valid-output fails explicitly and does not retry automatically. Please see the full release notes.

announcements.title: v2.5.1: Upgrade failures fixed (new China-reachable mirror source added); EAC cards no longer show the org prefix
announcements.html:
Fixed "check for updates" failing. On some networks raw.githubusercontent.com and cdn.jsdelivr.net are slow or intermittently unreachable, and the upgrade check would report no manifest source answered. This version adds a raw.githubusercontent.com proxy mirror for both the upgrade manifest and the announcement feed (measured at about 1.3 seconds returning the same bytes, while a single direct fetch from the source could take 16 seconds and time out).

The mirror does not fetch from a mutable branch: like the direct source, it first resolves to a full commit SHA, then fetches the manifest and each file by SHA; signature and per-file SHA-256 verification run as usual.

The small print on EAC cards no longer shows the org/ prefix (e.g. deepseek-v4.1-flash-free); the name line still shows EAC DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free. At the same time, the server-side EAC channel's external model names have been changed back to the prefixed form, and the Pinned / NEW / Hot / High-speed tags, 1M context and thinking levels are now all in effect.

Please check for updates to 2.5.1 in Settings → Plugin Upgrade.

announcements.title: v2.5.0: Free-lane 403 fixed (session ID encoding validation); recommended projects add EAC-design-world
announcements.html:
The free-lane 403 is fixed. From 2026-10-17 the upstream added encoding validation for session IDs: the twelve hex digits must be the official client's descending timestamp (~(milliseconds << 12 | counter), counter 1–63, the low twelve bits landing in 0xfc0–0xfff). Ascending forms or hash digests all get 403 FreeTierError.

The plugin now validates session IDs by encoding, and deterministically re-encodes a non-descending ID passed in by the caller into the compliant shape instead of passing it through as-is — the same conversation still corresponds to the same upstream session. Measured on the same IP: the original ascending ID got 403, the re-encoded one got 200.

The recommended projects page adds a third project: EAC-design-world — a local video production and design plugin for DeepSeek Harness: multi-track editing, templates and design systems, a native preview canvas, real file export, all done on the local machine. If it is useful to you, give it a Star while you are there.

The plugin, standalone local service and Windows desktop shell are all upgraded to 2.5.0. Please check for updates in Settings → Plugin Upgrade.

announcements.title: Free-lane 403 fixed: session ID encoding validation; EAC free models move to the server IP pool
announcements.html:
The free lane is usable again. From 2026-10-17 the upstream added encoding validation for session IDs, no longer looking only at the ses_ shape: the twelve hex digits must be a descending timestamp (~(milliseconds << 12 | counter), counter 1–63, the low twelve bits landing in 0xfc0–0xfff). Ascending forms or hash digests all get 403 FreeTierError.

Fixed in the plugin: session IDs are now validated by encoding, and a non-descending ID passed in by the caller is deterministically re-encoded into the compliant shape instead of being passed through as-is — the same conversation still corresponds to the same upstream session. Measured on the same IP: the original ascending ID got 403, the re-encoded one got 200.

EAC free models move to a server-side IP pool: an anonymous-lane gateway is deployed on the server, egress rotates through a free proxy pool (live nodes auto-refreshed every 30 minutes), so per-IP rate limits no longer affect availability; the EAC channel's deepseek-v4.1-flash-free and glm-5.3-flash-free have been switched to this chain, with all 20 consecutive requests succeeding.

Please upgrade the plugin and use it.

announcements.title: Two new OpenCode free models on the EAC channel: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free and GLM 5.3 Flash Free
announcements.html:
Two new models are now live via the EAC channel, forwarded by the OpenCode free lane, ranked at the very front of the EAC model page, with red NEW / Hot badges and a "High-speed" tag:

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free (opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free)
Supports image input; thinking levels are Off / Low / High / Max — "Off" genuinely takes effect (reasoning tokens go to zero), and all four levels are sent directly upstream.

GLM 5.3 Flash Free (opencode/glm-5.3-flash-free)
Natively multimodal (image / video / PDF); thinking levels are the three Low / High / Max, likewise genuinely sent.

Both models are forwarded with signatures through the server-side EAC gateway and do not affect the free lane; before use, complete the GitHub authorization and star the repository as the EAC channel requires.

announcements.title: v2.4.0: Free lane aligned with the OpenCode v2 client fingerprint; recommended projects page; aggregate channel row corrected
announcements.html:
Free lane: the fingerprint is redone to the upstream's v2 client in effect from 2026-10-14 — the User-Agent becomes opencode/latest/2.0.26/cli, the session headers gain four same-valued mirrors and drop the v1-only x-opencode-request, the tool gate becomes the two names read/shell with definitions aligned verbatim with the official client, and tool_choice: none is no longer sent. If the caller happens to use these two names, they are renamed to _client and restored on the response side.

Recommended projects page: the settings page adds a "Recommended Projects" page, with two cards pointing to EAC-Desktop and EAC-Pack; Star / Fork / recent commit counts are fetched live from GitHub, and if they cannot be fetched the whole block is not shown — placeholder numbers are never used.

Aggregate channels: the OpenCode password-free pool row is removed — it requires a per-request session fingerprint, which the aggregate lane's generic transport cannot carry; these 10 models are natively provided in the free lane anyway. The registry now shows 75 providers.

The plugin, standalone local service and Windows desktop shell are all upgraded to 2.4.0. Please check for updates in Settings → Plugin Upgrade.

announcements.title: Recommended projects page is live: EAC-Desktop, EAC-Pack and EAC-design-world — if they are useful, give them a Star
announcements.html:
The settings page adds a "Recommended Projects" page: three open-source projects from the same origin as this plugin — they put the Agent into a native desktop, let a hundred-plus plugins coexist in harmony, and keep video and design on this machine; they are also the desktop workbench behind the EAC co-paid channel. If they are useful to you, give them a Star while you are there.

EAC-Desktop · Desktop workbench
A Tauri native desktop based on DeepSeek Harness: bundled Node runtime, double-click to start working; project files, session changes, the plugin marketplace and skins all in one place, with installers for Windows / Linux / macOS.
github.com/Ebony-Vinyl/EAC-Desktop · Download and install

EAC-Pack · Plugin integration pack
DSH Desktop's plugin catalogue and batch install / update management: 72 built-in baseline sub-plugins, skin previews and a Prompt collection, with a pinned digest manifest verified byte-by-byte, so the installed environment is complete and trustworthy.
github.com/Ebony-Vinyl/EAC-Pack

EAC-design-world · Design workbench
DSH's local video production and design plugin: multi-track editing, templates and design systems, a native preview canvas, and exports that are real files; materials and projects stay on your own hard drive throughout.
github.com/Ebony-Vinyl/EAC-design-world

All three projects are free, open-source and ad-free. A Star is their only "pay slip" — every additional Star gives the author one more reason to keep the project going.

announcements.title: v2.3.0: Free-lane migration and the plugin upgrade page made independent
announcements.html:
Free lane: requests migrate to the new /inference/v1 path, with session identifiers, tool fingerprints and client attribution completed; session mappings are persisted and no longer lost when the service restarts. An upstream FreeTierError is now shown explicitly as a lane lock, instead of misleading users into signing in repeatedly.

Plugin upgrade: the upgrade feature becomes an independent navigation page, centrally showing version, progress and failure reasons; the settings page no longer shows the upgrade panel redundantly.

The plugin, standalone local service and Windows desktop shell are all upgraded to 2.3.0. Please check for updates in Settings → Plugin Upgrade; standalone-service and desktop users should use the full new program.

announcements.title: v2.1.0: Aggregate API — bring your own Key to access 76 providers; Token savers (tool output compression measured to save 90%); automatic fallback chain; native /v1/messages
announcements.html:
Aggregate API: the settings page adds "Aggregate Channels" — enter your own Key to merge 76 providers (NVIDIA NIM, OpenRouter, Groq, Cerebras, Gemini, DeepSeek, local Ollama, etc.) into the same model list, served externally through the local gateway together with the free lanes. Keys exist only in a local file at 0600, and the UI echoes only the last four digits.

Token savers: adds a "Token Savers" page. Tool output compression rewrites git diff / grep / ls / build logs and the like into shorter text with the same information content — measured to save 90% of the bytes on a 40 KB diff; there are also restrained prompt levels (concise / ultra-concise) and five local replies that "answer without calling a model" (quota probes, command prefixes, titles, suggestions, file paths), with a cumulative savings panel.

Automatic fallback chain: adds a "Routing" page, arranging several models into a chain (subscription → cheap → free). The first model in the chain that produces text is the answer; when it is rate-limited, refuses, or 5xxes midway, it automatically switches to the next, and the switch happens before any content is delivered, so no seam is visible in the conversation.

Local gateway: adds native Anthropic /v1/messages and /v1/messages/count_tokens; Claude Code and the Anthropic SDK can connect directly, without an OpenAI translation layer; the "Access" section of the settings page generates configuration snippets for Claude Code, Codex, the OpenAI SDK, the Anthropic SDK and curl from the actual port and Key.

announcements.title: v2.0.0: Big upgrade to the free channels — Kilo lane live; EAC adopts GitHub authorization (sign-in + Star); sign-in chain hardened
announcements.html:
Free channels: thirteen account channels adopted at once, a new Kilo lane; the channel list switches to real logos, with a live balance per account, automatic check-in, and the account-pool hero section restored.

EAC co-paid channel: now requires GitHub sign-in and starring the repository to use (one-click authorization on the settings page, the browser returns it automatically); removing the star invalidates it at the periodic recheck; the free lanes are completely unaffected. The sign-in chain is hardened: token claiming is idempotent, a gateway restart no longer swallows a completed sign-in, and failures say so plainly instead of spinning forever.

Fixes: self-update activation/rollback/recovery state (#93); nameless tool-call poisoning (#92) and old-kernel fallback (#89); EAC open to the web side (#58/#59); long conversations no longer intercepted by the front WAF (#63); long turns no longer cut when the account pool is saturated (#69/#70). EAC authorization enforcement is on: from now on, without signing in and starring the repository you will not be able to use EAC models; after upgrading, complete GitHub sign-in on the settings page.

announcements.title: v1.5.0: EAC channel adopts GitHub authorization (sign-in + Star required to use); free lanes unaffected
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.5.0 adds a per-person authorization gate to the EAC co-paid channel: sign in with GitHub and give the repository a Star to use EAC models.

  • Why — EAC is a co-paid lane whose capacity follows this repository's Star count (per 1 Star, account pool +1.5). Binding usage rights to Stars aligns "the people who use it" with "the people who sustain the capacity".
  • How to use it — Settings → Our Free Model → EAC Channel Authorization → "Sign in with GitHub": the browser automatically opens the authorization page; after signing in and starring, return to the app and you are done, with no copy-pasting of anything — the plugin completes claiming automatically; if you have not starred yet, the authorization page offers "I have starred it, recheck", with no need to sign in again.
  • Removing the Star invalidates it — the server rechecks the Star every 12 hours; after removal, authorization expires within the recheck window. A GitHub-side failure or rate limit keeps the existing authorization and causes no false harm.
  • The free lanes are completely unaffected — the opencode lane's models do not go through the server, need no sign-in and no Star, and work as usual.
  • Transition period — this version is first in a compatibility window (EAC remains usable without sign-in); a separate announcement will precede formal enforcement; we recommend completing sign-in early to avoid interruption when the time comes.
  • Privacy — only the minimal read:user scope is requested, used only for Star verification; authorization exists only on your machine and the server, and you can sign out at any time on the settings page (revoked immediately on the server side).

All offline suites (including the new authorization gate suite) pass, and the manifest is re-signed byte-by-byte. Please go to Settings → Plugin Upgrade for the one-click upgrade.

announcements.title: v1.4.7: Long-turn time limits relaxed — normal long-thinking turns no longer cut when the account pool is saturated (#69/#70)
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.4.7 fixes the problem reported in #69/#70: long-thinking turns truncated by STREAM_CUT at exactly 8 minutes.

  • Whole-turn limit 480→900 seconds, recovery segment 180→300 seconds — the previous 8-minute wall-clock cap would reliably cut normal long turns when the account pool was saturated (measured 1923 capacity / 2451 concurrency, first token 34–220 seconds, deep thinking over 6 minutes): in the field, "deep in thought, 6 min 16 sec elapsed" was immediately followed by reached its 480s time limit. With the relaxation, such turns can run to completion normally.
  • The anti-hang semantics are unchanged — the transport layer has a separate 300-second idle cutoff for "no bytes at all" (reset by every data chunk), and the wall clock only backstops turns that "keep producing frames but are overall very slow"; values may still only be adjusted downwards, and a whole turn still makes at most two physical requests.

The actual speed of long turns still depends on queueing in the upstream shared account pool; a low thinking level can significantly shorten the wait. Please go to Settings → Plugin Upgrade for the one-click upgrade.

announcements.title: v1.4.6: EAC co-paid channel open to the web side (#58/#59); long conversations no longer intercepted by the front WAF (#63); error classification no longer misleads into re-signing in
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.4.6, a focused round on the issue tracker:

  • EAC co-paid channel open to the web side (#58/#59/#61) — the host gate adds kernel-declared web profiles (web / web-desktop): the "Deepseek Harness EAC" desktop shell using the web-desktop profile and the dsh web combination can now see the six EAC models; the channel credentials' sealing and signing mechanism is preserved as-is. A completely unrecognizable host remains hidden, but the model list on the settings page now shows an explicit note instead of a silent absence (#60).
  • Long conversations no longer intercepted by the front WAF (#63) — the server side has added /eac/v1/ to the front WAF's URL allowlist: previously a long-conversation request body over 200,000 characters would be stopped by an "Nginx buffer overflow" page (370 times in one day at peak), and now these requests go straight to the signing gateway. The plugin side is hardened in sync: HTML error pages returned by front proxies (WAF / CDN) are uniformly simplified to one readable line of copy naming the real cause; a WAF 403 page is no longer misdiagnosed as "credentials invalid", leading you to sign in repeatedly; the HTML folding path under a 200 status becomes non-retryable, no longer automatically hammering the same over-long request three times.
  • A conclusion on first-token latency and one addition (#66) — measurements and server logs together prove: the signing lane, SSE keepalive and concurrency gates are all normal throughout, and the 34–221-second first-token wait comes from queueing in the relay upstream's shared account pool (the upstream's roughly 800 channels average a 32.5-second response, with slow channels over 2 minutes). On the plugin side, pass-through of thinking frames spelled thinking is added: once a turn on a slow channel starts producing frames, the thinking content is no longer lost. For the wait on slow channels themselves, please use a low thinking level to mitigate it.
  • Upgrade trust chain catch-up (#64) — the problem where the 1.4.5 manifest drifted by 1 byte in each of 4 files due to a repository-rename commit, causing all "one-click upgrades" from old versions to fail, was fixed when the 1.4.5 manifest was re-signed; this release passes the manifest consistency check and the full-chain upgrade test against the real manifest as usual.

All offline suites pass, the manifest is re-signed byte-by-byte; the WAF allowlist change was verified with real signed requests (both 64KB and 300KB request bodies reached the gateway directly), and other sites on the same machine are unaffected. Please go to Settings → Plugin Upgrade for the one-click upgrade.

announcements.title: v1.4.5: Egress proxy live (subscription / single proxy) — EAC signing lane hardened, truncated answers auto-continued, settings page sub-path fixed
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.4.5, a maintenance consolidation: friends in restricted regions or on unstable routes get an egress proxy, and a batch of concentrated real-world failures is fixed at the same time.

  • Egress proxy (subscription / single proxy) — the plugin's upstream requests can now go through your own egress: an airport subscription (automatically starts a local mihomo, speed-tests and picks the best node, kicks out 429 nodes) or a single HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy. The settings page shows the current best node and its access latency; subscription addresses are treated as credentials and read only when you click "Show". Upgrades / announcements / the EAC lane do not go through the egress, isolating the fault domain.
  • EAC signing lane hardened — the signed request body is now sent directly via Node's core http(s) module, so local plugins that rewrite fetch, such as billion-context, can no longer touch the signed bytes; previously a gateway report of "request signature rejected" was misdiagnosed as invalid credentials, and now it clearly indicates a local proxy rewrite (#50).
  • Settings page cannot reach the backend — deployments mounted under a reverse-proxy sub-path no longer lose the prefix; the desktop side's dsh-app:// relay request admission compatibility is merged from a community PR, with admission anomalies converted to 503 and fixed-field diagnostic logs emitted (#49/#54).
  • Truncated answers auto-continued — when an answer hits the output cap and is truncated, the plugin feeds the already-produced body back in and auto-continues once, so you no longer need to send "continue" manually (#28).
  • Dashboard — adds an account-pool load panel (capacity, 24h active, in-flight concurrency; the smooth/busy/overloaded verdict is given in real time by the gateway process, all numbers real) and a one-line summary of "the most recent turn" (#26).
  • Gateway default per-IP concurrency 20→5 — one LLM stream holds an upstream connection for tens of seconds to minutes, and the old default let a single user fill the shared lane and drag down the whole machine (one of the #55 field cases).

All offline suites pass, the manifest is re-signed byte-by-byte; the local gateway and real-machine self-checks (chat / tools / vision / update chain) are all green. Please go to Settings → Plugin Upgrade for the one-click upgrade.

announcements.title: v1.4.4: DeepSeek's leaked DSML control markers stripped — <｜DSML｜ calls> no longer shown after thinking ends
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.4.4 fixes a display defect of the DeepSeek V4-series models: in some turns, at the moment the model finishes thinking and is about to call a tool, it leaks its internal control marker <｜DSML｜ calls> as body text (that server-side sample did not intercept this special token), so users would see this garbled string at the start of the answer.

  • Streaming stripping — the plugin's stream parser now strips <｜DSML｜…> control fragments from the visible body in real time (a half marker is buffered until it can be judged before being emitted); genuine tool-call frames are unaffected and tools execute as usual.
  • Both lanes take effect together — the free lane and the EAC channel use the same parser; the EAC channel's six DeepSeek/Kimi/GLM models are likewise protected.
  • The three-retry upgrade download from 1.4.3 is kept as-is.

All 21 offline suites pass, and the manifest is Ed25519-re-signed byte-by-byte. Please go to Settings → Plugin Upgrade for the one-click upgrade.

announcements.title: v1.4.3: Upgrade downloads retry three times per file — a transient break no longer fails the whole package upgrade
announcements.html: Our Free Model v1.4.3 fixes the upgrade chain itself: upgrade downloads retry three times per file. A user upgrading from 1.3.1 → 1.4.2 hit staging failed: …: fetch failed — connections from domestic egress to the CDN jitter momentarily, and staging previously gave each file only one chance, so one jitter failed the whole package. Now transport failures (connection cut, timeout, 5xx/429) automatically back off and retry twice; integrity failures (size / SHA-256 mismatch) are still refused on the first try — that is the trust chain refusing, leaving nothing to luck. All 21 offline suites pass, and the manifest is Ed25519-re-signed byte-by-byte. If an upgrade fails, just click "Upgrade now" again; from 1.4.3 it withstands transient jitter itself.

announcements.title: v1.4.2: EAC co-paid channel live (six flagships · 1M context · vision); signing gateway and seven gates measured; thinking levels; contributor 8 PRs merged
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.4.2 brings all the accumulation since the September release in one go: a new EAC co-paid channel, the signing gateway and anti-abuse gates behind it, and contributors' 8 PRs.

  • EAC co-paid channel (desktop only) — adds six flagship models: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (1M context · vision · thinking Off/Low/High/Extreme · 384K output), Kimi K3 (1M · vision · strong reasoning · Agentic), Kimi K2.6 (262K · vision), GLM-5.3 / GLM-5.3 Flash (1M · deep thinking), GPT-OSS 20B (open weights). Channel credentials are sealed in the plugin in three shards with AES-256-GCM, derived at runtime via HKDF; the host gate confirms the desktop side before unlocking (the web profile has 0 EAC model rows), and when locked, LANE_LOCKED fails once with no retry storm.
  • Signing gateway: keys never leave the server — the relay's real key lives only in the gateway environment; plugin requests carry an HMAC-SHA256 signature (replay window ±600s, constant-time comparison, multi-key rotation in parallel, only two routes allowed). SSE prelude: as soon as signature verification passes it returns 200 + stream head + keepalive heartbeat, so a reasoning model's 20–140s first-token wait is no longer cut by nginx 60s / Cloudflare 100s (a measured 124-second GLM-5.3 completed in full); upstream refusals travel as in-stream error frames, classified as before.
  • Seven anti-abuse gates measured — no signature / forged / replay 401, outside-allowlist 403, over 8MB 413, unknown route 404, 61 requests/minute 429, every gate verified with real requests; plus 20 concurrency/IP + model allowlist + Cloudflare edge; the gateway dashboard accounts IPs by salted hash, and the New API panel sidebar automatically mounts an "EAC Dashboard" entry.
  • Thinking control — the level menu copies ZCode's model declarations (DeepSeek Off/Low/High/Extreme, Kimi Low/High/Extreme, GLM Low/High/Extreme, GPT-OSS Low/Medium/High), and the default level must be inside its own menu; EAC requests carry an anti-overthinking system prompt, with silent turns auto-continued as a backstop.
  • Contributor PRs merged — #23/#24/#25/#27/#35/#36/#37/#38/#39: forwarding LAN relay, sync dual-start race, port step-up notices, refusal/pause_turn continuation, etc.
  • Experience details — front-proxy HTML error pages are simplified to one readable line of copy; the free lane's rate-limit badge becomes "Temporarily unavailable" (it was always fluctuation in the upstream public pool, not your quota).

All 21 offline suites pass, and the manifest is Ed25519-re-signed byte-by-byte. The EAC channel is visible only on the dsh desktop side; please go to Settings → Plugin Upgrade for the one-click upgrade.

announcements.title: v1.3.2: Self-update trust chain signed (#19); forwarding-port tool calls fixed (#20/#21); quota backoff (#13); heatmap tiles merged (#11)
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.3.2 handles five items from the issue tracker:

  • Self-update trust chain re-rooted (#19) — previously the upgrade manifest was just a bare JSON pulled over HTTPS, with file hashes written in the manifest, so whoever forged the manifest forged the hashes along with it; jsDelivr, a third-party CDN, was also in the trust chain. Now every manifest must carry an Ed25519 signature from the release private key, with the public key pinned in the plugin and the private key not in the repository: a poisoned mirror (including jsDelivr) can only cause the upgrade to fail, no longer to become code execution. The feedUrl setting is fully decoupled from update sources (it only redirects announcements); the manifest base allows only relative paths; plugin API request bodies gain a 1MB cap; the forwarding listener now binds by DNS resolution and requires full loopback, so a hosts file pointing localhost at a routable interface can no longer leak quota.
  • Tool calls under the forwarding port fixed (#20/#21) — streaming tool_calls[].index previously shared a counter with reasoning blocks, so the first tool call often arrived at index 2+, and clients accumulating by index got a holed array with parameters merged and lost; now calls are renumbered from 0. When the model calls the decoy tools bash/read/grep appended to pass the fingerprint gate (the Unknown tool 'bash' reported in #21 is exactly them), the call is suppressed block-by-block at the forwarding port, no longer handing the client a tool it never registered. A tool-argument turn truncated by the output cap also truthfully returns length in streaming. /v1/responses supports instructions/max_output_tokens/streaming, and streaming output_index no longer collides.
  • The at-quota experience (#13) — the lane's 429 carries an increasing retry-after, and the plugin previously also auto-retried twice, turning one wall into three; now a 429 is reported on the spot. After a whole round of availability probing returns all 429s, it backs off exponentially from 30→120 minutes (manual reprobe, egress changes and startup rounds are unlimited), so probing no longer fights your turns for the same per-IP-counted pool. The speed-test button uses the default level and relaxes the frontend timeout, no longer almost certain to fail while also burning quota.
  • Heatmap tiles merged (#11) — cell gap zeroed, corner radius shrunk, for a coherent GitHub contribution-graph feel.
  • Other — the frontend relaxes timeouts by route (speed test 240s, upgrade 600s); after an announcement push disconnects it reconnects with 30s→5min backoff instead of failing permanently; a completed upgrade clears the old error banner; a store write failure is said once in the log.

All 20 offline suites and tsc --noEmit pass, with installation and upgrade-chain acceptance completed on a real dsh host. Please go to Settings → Plugin Upgrade for the one-click upgrade.

announcements.title: v1.3.1: Tool results finally delivered to the model (#9); cut-off long thinking no longer counts as success (#10); upstream sources written into the README (#8)
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.3.1 handles three items from the issue tracker:

  • Tool calls and tool results were not sent to the model (#9) — dsh used two message shapes across two generations to record tool results: before V4 it was a user message with a tool-result content block, and from V4 it is a role:'tool' message. The plugin recognized only the latter, so on the dsh 0.1.5 / AIO 6.9.3 generation of kernels, every agent task on the free lane could not send out tool results: the model repeatedly issued the same call, insisting "the image read returned no content", until you stopped it manually. Now both shapes are recognized and projected onto the three wire formats, and images embedded in tool results are no longer dropped. The same round carries an accompanying fix: the bash decoy tool appended to pass the free-tier fingerprint gate would really be called by the model (24 times in one session, all unknown tool), and now the kernel's real shell tool (called pwsh on Windows in this generation) is promoted to occupy that name, and restored to the real tool name when the call returns, so it is executable.
  • A stream closed early by the upstream was treated as finishing normally (#10) — when the gateway closed the SSE stream having sent neither a finish token nor a usage frame, the plugin fell back to stop, so a turn where "the model thought for five minutes and then went silent" was marked complete, with statistics still showing ok:true / 0 tokens. Now this is judged a failure on the spot: the UI writes "this turn's run failed" and at which second the truncation happened, and the statistics row leaves truncated and noUsage for audit. A resend is reserved only for truncations where "not a single token came out" — measured in a real dsh web session: this lane reliably cuts pure-thinking turns at 304 seconds, and with the code then retryable, the harness resent the same five-minute answer twice (llm/retry landing at 304s and 608s, turn/end at 912s), three identical failures, fifteen minutes, and still no answer in the end. The cap is brought by this turn's length, not network jitter, and resending cannot stop it.
  • Upstream sources written into the README (#8) — adds an "Which sources are upstream" section: there is only one, OpenCode's Zen gateway (https://opencode.ai), using its public password-free quota, with no third-party relay or account pool; there are four classes of egress targets in total, listed item by item.

Cross-validated on real session records from both the dsh 0.1.5 and 0.1.7 kernel generations. Please go to Settings → Plugin Upgrade for the one-click upgrade.

announcements.title: v1.3.0: New managed installation mode, adapting to the ecosystem integration pack; forwarding port repeated restarts fixed
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.3.0 prepares for entry into the EAC ecosystem integration pack:

  • Managed installation mode (distribution=managed) — when the plugin is taken over by an integration pack / package manager, in-app self-upgrade, the announcement source and hot reload all shut down (the corresponding endpoints return 409), and release bytes and update timing are handed to the managing party; the settings interface cannot reverse the managed state. Self-installed users are completely unaffected.
  • Upstream kernel dependency converged to adapter/ — the only place in the whole package allowed to import @deepseek-ai/* is adapter/kernel.js; every other module references it through the seam, solidified by a test gate, preventing upstream coupling from spreading again.
  • Forwarding port repeated restarts fixed — previously every save on the settings page restarted a local forwarding service whose host:port was already satisfied once, and the Bearer copied out by clients would expire with it; now, when the expectation is already satisfied, the existing service is reused directly.
  • Catalogue and integrity records — adds manifest 0.15 catalogue records (catalog/dsh-plugin.json), provenance and integrity manifests, all SHA-256 generated by the build script from the actual bytes after LF normalization, with no placeholder or fabricated values.

Self-installed users, please go to Settings → Plugin Upgrade for the one-click upgrade; managed-install users' update cadence is arranged by the integration pack.

announcements.title: v1.2.2: One-click upgrade fixed; thinking levels raised per model; unavailable models no longer enter the picker
announcements.html:
Our Free Model v1.2.2 handles the issues on the tracker one by one:

  • In-app upgrade usable again (#1) — the 1.2.1 release manifest did not match the actual files, so any old version clicking "One-click upgrade" would fail at the verification stage. The manifest has been regenerated with the version, and a new build-manifest.mjs --check is added: if the manifest does not match the real files it exits non-zero, already wired into npm test and CI.
  • Models whose thinking cannot be turned off are no longer truncated frequently (#2) — models like MiMo V2.6 share one quota between thinking and body text, so the three levels are raised overall to 4 096 / 16 384 / the model cap; the explanatory text on every model card and thinking level on the settings page is now generated from the numbers actually sent, so "the UI says 8K, it actually sends 16K" no longer occurs.
  • Models probed as unavailable no longer enter the picker (#3) — only when the gateway explicitly names "this id is not routed" is it removed from the dropdown, with the refusal reason kept on the settings page; 5xx, rate limits, timeouts and network cuts are no longer treated as a verdict on the model, and models not yet probed on a fresh install remain selectable as usual.
  • A composition without a browser UI can also install (#4) — the plugin treats only the model lanes as a hard dependency; the settings page's other half hangs on its own fiber and mounts when the web service appears, so models come out fine in an environment with no web server. (Not yet verified on a real dsh-tui environment.)
  • Streaming responses recognized by body, not header (#6) — under high load the gateway will reply with a whole set of SSE frames under an application/json content-type; now this is judged by the response body's shape, sniffed bytes are fed back into the stream, so it neither errors out the whole turn nor misjudges a usable model as unavailable.

Old-version users, please go to Settings → Plugin Upgrade for the one-click upgrade; new-install users need do nothing. (The multi-egress node polling proposed in #5 is out of scope.)
